The programme tests two claims: that next-token prediction is computed over a prompt-induced structure rather than selected over the model's whole learned content, and that there are portable viewpoint directions — operators that change how a subject is rendered while leaving what is rendered intact.

## Negatives

Given equal prominence, on purpose — a null with its diagnosis is the part that's checkable.

**Anisotropy null.** [fill in — what broke, and what rule came out of it]

**Persona-decay readout.** Failed once piloted against data already on disk, before any new run was built on it. Rule: no experiment gets built until its readout has been piloted on existing data.

**v1 gate.** Used an absolute threshold with no control null, so it couldn't distinguish a real effect from noise. Rule: gate on a control-referenced z-score, never an absolute threshold.

## Methods {#methods}

Standing rules for everything on this page: a pre-registered dev gate before a run counts; held-out topics and held-out wordings, never reused from estimation; effects reported against a control-referenced z-score rather than an absolute threshold; no experiment built until its readout has been piloted on data already on disk.

All scripts live in one public repo, fixed seeds, one script per experiment: [repo link]. Every card above links to its own script and saved outputs.
